  • Build durable, replayable event-processing pipelines and asynchronous job execution platforms that other product teams compose to ship features faster.
  • Design and operate caching, rate-limiting, and request-shaping layers that protect upstream systems and enable safe scaling under bursty workloads.
  • Develop platform abstractions, SDKs, and paved-road libraries that codify best practices and let product teams consume capabilities without re-implementing them.

  • Partner with infrastructure, security, and SRE teams to ensure platform services meet enterprise reliability, compliance, and security obligations.

  • Advanced proficiency in at least one major backend language such as Java, Go, Scala, Rust, or modern C++.
  • Deep understanding of high-throughput messaging, streaming, and event-driven architectures using technologies such as Kafka, Pulsar, or NATS.
  • Strong working knowledge of data storage systems across relational, key-value, document, and search workloads.

jobs.description:
Established in 2015, Create Music Group is a leading music and entertainment company. The company operates as a record label, distribution company, and entertainment network which generates over 15 billion music streams each month on DSP’s. Named #2 on the Inc 5000 Fastest Growth Companies in America in 2020, the company has grown exponentially by leveraging its owned IP with its media and technology platform. The company works with superstar artists, major and independent record labels, and global media brands. It operates a number of companies including Label Engine, one of the largest independent music distribution platforms in the world, with over 75,000 artists and 5,000 label clients; and Flighthouse, a digital entertainment brand focused on Gen Z, which has more than 300 million followers across social media. Create Music Group is based in Hollywood, CA and has 400 employees worldwide.

Job Summary

The Publishing Onboarding Manager runs assigned publishing catalog transitions end to end, from deal handoff through steady-state administration. Executes the standard onboarding playbook across catalog ingestion, registration, and works delivery to societies, sub-publishers, and digital endpoints, and owns the identification and redirection of rights and royalty streams for assigned catalogs. Serves as day-to-day operational contact for partners and sellers, coordinating with M&A, Royalties, Business Affairs, and Legal throughout each transition. Reports to the Publishing Onboarding Director.

Responsibilities

  • Owns the operational onboarding of assigned catalogs end to end, from deal handoff through absorption into steady-state administration and collection, executing the standard playbook at every stage.
  • Turns deal diligence materials into a transition plan with named owners and deadlines within five business days of handoff, and keeps partners, sellers, and internal teams on schedule against it.
  • Serves as the day-to-day operational contact for partners and sellers on assigned transitions, running onboarding calls, setting documentation expectations early, and escalating to the Director when partners are missing records or administrative know-how.
  • Executes catalog ingestion for assigned deals: validates schedules of works, identifiers (ISRC, IPI, ISWC), and ownership splits against deal schedules, and resolves metadata gaps and chain-of-title conflicts before works are registered and delivered.
  • Executes registration and works delivery for assigned catalogs to societies, sub-publishers, and digital endpoints including YouTube, including CWR submission, acknowledgement processing, and remediation of non-accepted works.

The Role:

Telecom is at an inflection point. Networks are getting smarter, customer expectations are outpacing legacy systems, and the pressure to monetize 5G while cutting operational costs has never been greater. This is where you come in.

As Director of Industry Marketing for Telecommunications, you'll own the narrative that makes ServiceNow irreplaceable to telco buyers. You know this industry—its pressures, its players, its language—and you know how to translate that knowledge into messaging that stops a CTO or VP of Operations mid-scroll and makes them say, "this is exactly what I need."

But here's what makes this role different: you're not just a storyteller. You're building an AI-first marketing motion—one where AI agents, automated content workflows, and intelligent buyer signals are baked into how your team operates every day.

What You'll Do

  • Own the industry narrative. Define ServiceNow's point of view for Telecom—crafting narratives that connect platform and portfolio capabilities to the real problems telco buying groups are solving right now: network operations transformation, BSS/OSS modernization, field service efficiency, and customer experience reinvention. Use AI to accelerate your industry research, synthesize competitive signals, and stress-test your messaging before it ever hits a sales deck.
  • Build buyer-specific messaging. Architect messaging tailored to distinct buyer personas—CIO, COO, Chief Network Officer, VP of Customer Operations—that moves from "we have a problem" to "ServiceNow is the answer." Leverage AI to generate, pressure-test, and rapidly iterate persona-specific content so your team ships more, faster, without sacrificing quality.
  • Set the AI-first standard across the team. Model what it looks like to use AI tools as a core part of the marketing workflow, not a nice-to-have. Coach your colleagues on how to build repeatable, AI-assisted content systems that scale your output and raise the quality bar across the board.
  • Drive pipeline, not just awareness. Partner closely with product marketing, Industry Go-to-Market, and field marketing to ensure industry narratives translate into pipeline-generating plays.
  • Run an AI-embedded content engine. Build thought leadership, executive briefs, event programming, and digital assets where AI is embedded in how content gets researched, drafted, personalized, and distributed. The expectation isn't just that you use AI—it's that your team can't imagine working without it.
  • Stay ahead of the industry. Track BSS/OSS players, hyperscaler partnerships, industry ecosystem dynamics, and the competitive landscape so your messaging is always credible and current. Use AI-powered listening and synthesis tools to monitor signals at a pace that would be impossible manually.
  • Represent ServiceNow externally. Show up at industry events, analyst briefings, and customer forums as a credible voice on telco transformation—and on what AI-powered marketing looks like in practice.

Why This Matters

Telcos are running some of the most complex operations on the planet—millions of customers, thousands of field technicians, aging infrastructure, and a mandate to transform while the lights stay on. The right narrative doesn't just win deals. It shifts how an entire industry thinks about what's possible. That's the opportunity in front of you.

To be successful in this role you have:

  • 12+ years of experience in B2B marketing, including 3–5+ years focused on the telecommunications industry or a similar vertical-specific marketing role.
  • Deep familiarity with the telecommunications industry—either from inside a telco, a key vendor in the ecosystem, or years of focused industry marketing coverage. You know what a telecom transformation really means, and you can talk to a network ops leader without a glossary.
  • Proven track record building industry or vertical marketing programs that influence pipeline—not just brand impressions.
  • A sharp instinct for buyer psychology: what keeps a telco executive up at night, what gets budget approved, and what makes a message land versus get ignored.
  • Experience translating complex platform capabilities into crisp, compelling narratives that resonate with business buyers (not just technical audiences).
  • You've fundamentally changed how you work in the last 12 months—and AI is why. You're not experimenting with AI on the side; it's how you research industries, stress-test messaging, generate first drafts, personalize at scale, and move faster than a team twice your size. You can speak specifically to how AI has reshaped your workflow, and you're actively raising the bar for the people around you.
  • You see AI as a strategic advantage, not a productivity shortcut. You understand how to prompt for insight, how to QA AI-generated content with a sharp editorial eye, and how to build repeatable AI-assisted content systems that your whole team can use.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills; you're comfortable influencing without authority across product, sales, and demand generation teams.

We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager to lead our growing full stack engineering team and help scale the technology powering Ledgebrook’s underwriting, policy, and data systems.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical acumen with strong people leadership — someone who can coach engineers, shape architecture, and partner with product to deliver at Ledgebrook speed. jobs.excerpt: Primary Function of PositionAs a senior technical leader within the Clinical Affairs department, the Lead Biostatistician (Biostatistician 5) sets the statistical vision and direction for the design, conduct, and analysis of clinical studies spanning early feasibility through pivotal pre-market trials and post-market evidence generation.
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position

As a senior technical leader within the Clinical Affairs department, the Lead Biostatistician (Biostatistician 5) sets the statistical vision and direction for the design, conduct, and analysis of clinical studies spanning early feasibility through pivotal pre-market trials and post-market evidence generation. The Biostatistician 5 operates as a fully independent statistical leader and the recognized go-to statistical authority across Clinical Affairs and beyond, staying abreast of the latest developments in the field and translating them into impactful improvements for the team. This role owns multiple business or functional areas and a portfolio of ten or more concurrent projects, sets the programming and analysis standards the department works to, develops the training curricula, SOPs, and work instructions that build capability across all levels of the function, and represents Intuitive Biostatistics directly with regulatory agencies, principal investigators, key opinion leaders, and the broader scientific community. This is an individual contributor role carrying substantial technical and strategic leadership expectations without direct people-management responsibility.

Roles & Responsibilities

Study Design & Protocol Development: Independently strategize and develop the statistical approach for complex clinical protocols, including Bayesian and frequentist design selection, endpoint and estimand framing, hypothesis tests, power analyses, sample size justification, randomization design & review, and adaptive and/or interim analysis strategy. Serve as the final internal statistical authority for design decisions across owned studies and advise on design trade-offs at the program and platform level. Serves Data Monitoring Committees (DMCs, DSMBs) as the unblinded sponsor statistician.

Statistical Analysis Plans & Mock TLFs: Set the vision and direction for Statistical Analysis Plans (SAPs) and mock Tables, Listings, and Figures (TLFs) across the portfolio, defining the standards, templates, and degree of pre-specification for the department. Review and approve SAPs and mock TLFs authored by others against those standards, balancing flexibility and consistency across studies.

Data Analysis: Set the vision and direction for the analysis of clinical trial data, selecting and championing the methodology applied across studies and ensuring analyses are reproducible, defensible, and of a quality that withstands regulatory and peer review. Personally own the most complex or novel analytical problems in the portfolio, and direct interim analyses, database lock, and unblinding activities per study requirements.

Portfolio Management: Manage a portfolio of 10 or more projects simultaneously and take ownership of multiple business or functional areas, setting priorities, sequencing work, and allocating statistical effort across them.

Clinical Operations Roadmap: Serve as the Biostatistics representative and strategic partner in core team and program-level forums, shaping evidence generation strategy across surgical specialties and product platforms, setting execution roadmaps, managing timelines and stakeholder expectations.

Team Communication: Act as an influential voice across Clinical Operations and beyond, with a reputation as the go-to statistician. Influence senior leadership as a key strategic thought partner, distilling statistical complexity into clear, actionable direction with explicit clinical and business implications. Lead meetings and set agendas for the biostatistics team.

Scientific Literature & Evidence Generation: Write or edit the methods, results, and interpretation sections for a portfolio of studies with strategic guidance to support regulatory submissions, compliance documents, scientific journals, and medical conferences. Lead additional research as needed to generate clinical evidence, such as analyses of large clinical or administrative databases, systematic literature reviews, and meta-analyses. Stay abreast of the latest developments in biostatistical methodology and translate them into impactful improvements to how the team designs, analyzes, and reports. Independently contribute to the scientific community through peer-reviewed publication, conference presentation, and methodological contribution.

External Engagement: Conduct independent, direct interactions representing Intuitive Biostatistics with regulatory agencies, Principal Investigators (PIs), Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), and external statisticians, including addressing regulatory authority questions on statistical design and analysis for pre-approval, post-approval, and post-market clinical follow-up studies. Sustain multiple external relationships and be regarded as a thought leader in the field.

Data Management Support: Co-strategize with Data Management to develop the direction for data quality, consistency, scalability, and traceability. Specify CDISC-aligned data structures (SDTM, ADaM) and establish analysis-ready dataset specifications.

Process Improvement & Departmental Standards: Set the vision for programming and analysis standards across the department, lead by example in own code and deliverables, and implement across the department. Develop and own SOPs and Work Instructions to drive standardization, validation, and quality control of analysis pipelines such that results meet rigorous standards for regulatory submission and scientific publication.

Mentorship & Capability Building: Set the training curriculum for the biostatistics team and deliver training on both biostatistics methodology and programming practice. Provide technical leadership and career-development guidance to statisticians at all junior levels, raising the technical ceiling of the department. Oversee and direct external statistical vendors and CROs.

Regulatory Compliance: Ensure all activities strictly adhere to Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ISO 14155, ICH E9, ICH E6, and 21 CFR Part 812 regulations. Apply situationally relevant FDA guidances including adaptive designs and Bayesian methods for medical device trials.

Qualifications

Skills, Experience, Education, & Training

Minimum Degree: Master's (MS) or Ph.D. in Biostatistics or Statistics.

Professional Experience: Minimum of 9 years of experience with an MS, or 6 years with a Ph.D.

Clinical Trial Experience: Minimum of 5 years of clinical trial experience required.

Medical Device Experience: Minimum of 5 years of medical device experience required; surgical and robotic-assisted device clinical research strongly preferred.

Statistical Methods: Track record of developing and applying industry-leading, innovative, and integrative biostatistical methodology to problems that standard approaches do not solve. Depth expected across several of: adaptive and group-sequential designs, Bayesian methods, use of historical or external controls, survival and longitudinal modeling, hierarchical models, multiplicity control, missing data and sensitivity analysis, and analysis of large real-world datasets.

Programming: Mastery of R required; SAS and Python additionally valued. Demonstrated ability to set programming standards for a team, write clean, functional, modular, well-tested code in a shared development environment, and lead by example in code review and validation practice. Fluent in version control (Git) in a GxP validated environment for reproducible analyses ready for regulatory compliance audits.

AI-Enabled Productivity: Proven experience applying frontier AI models to dramatically expand the productivity of the biostatistician job function as a whole, beyond personal use. Candidates must be able to point to specific, verifiable examples of workflows they have re-engineered with frontier models, and to quantify the resulting gains in cycle time, throughput, or quality. The successful candidate will be expected to drive adoption across the biostatistics team by establishing the patterns, tooling, and human-in-the-loop verification controls that make AI-assisted work reliable, reproducible, and compliant in an international GxP environment.

Independence & Leadership: Fully independent operation with substantial leadership scope, including the ability to set direction for others, resolve ambiguity without escalation, and be held accountable for the technical quality of a multi-project portfolio.

External Reputation: Established reputation and multiple sustained relationships within the external scientific (biostatistics, medical devices, clinical trials) and regulatory community, with a record of independent contribution to that community.

Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication, teamwork, and interpersonal skills with technical and non-technical constituents, including senior leadership and external audiences. Strong scientific writing and editing skills, high attention to detail, and unwavering scientific integrity.

Logistics

Location: Remote OK. Preference will be given to candidates able to be onsite in Sunnyvale, California or willing to relocate.

Travel: Up to 10%.

jobs.description:
Senior Financial Analyst, FP&A (AI First)

Department: Operations

Location: Remote, Canada or US

Position Type: Full-Time, Permanent

Hours: Monday-Friday, 9AM-5PM (in your time zone)

About the Role

Unbounce is looking for a Senior Financial Analyst, FP&A (AI First) to join our FP&A team. You'll run our budgeting and forecasting cycles, prepare monthly reporting, support the accounting team through month-end close, and partner with teams across the business to answer financial questions.

This is an AI-native role: the outputs are familiar (an annual budget, a rolling forecast, a monthly reporting package, board metrics), but you will spend a meaningful share of your time building the systems that produce them rather than producing them by hand. Every employee at Unbounce has Claude, and our billing and accounting stack was rebuilt this year on Recurly and Rillet, so the data layer underneath you is new rather than inherited.

Concretely, when a recurring analysis takes four hours by hand, we expect your instinct to be to build the thing that does it in four minutes next month, and then to be the person who can tell whether its answer is right. The second half matters more than the first. Automation without judgment is worse than no automation, and this role owns both.

We're after someone dependable and detail-oriented who communicates clearly and whose first instinct on a repetitive task is to automate it. You don't need to have done every item on this list. If you're strong in most areas and willing to learn the rest, we'd like to hear from you.

What You’ll Be Doing

Build and operate AI-driven finance workflows

  • Design, build and maintain the AI agents and automated workflows that carry the recurring FP&A load: variance analysis, first-pass commentary, cohort and retention analysis, board metric refreshes, and the routine data pulls underneath all of them.
  • Use AI as a default part of your workflow, across analysis, modeling, reporting, and commentary, within our team practices and data-handling guidelines.
  • Use Claude, which every employee here already has, to speed up analysis, automate recurring reporting, draft first-pass variance commentary, and pressure-test your own assumptions before numbers go out.
  • Build the context these agents need in order to be reliable: metric definitions, documented data lineage from source system to report, and explicit rules for how each number is constructed. An agent is only as good as the context it can reach.
  • Decide what should and should not be automated. Draw and defend the line between work an agent runs unsupervised, work an agent drafts for human review, and work that stays fully manual.
  • Own the finance team's shared library of agents, prompts, skills and calculation templates. Treat it as a deliverable in its own right, versioned and documented, so that it keeps producing when you are on vacation.
  • Own what the tools produce, review AI-assisted work to the same standard as your own, and know when a question needs judgment instead. Build the checks in: validation against source, reconciliation, and a review step that catches a wrong answer before it reaches leadership or the board.
  • Raise the ceiling for the people around you. Some of your highest-leverage work will be enabling your business partners to answer their own questions rather than producing the analysis yourself.

Planning and forecasting

  • Prepare Own the annual budget and quarterly/monthly forecast updates, gathering inputs from department leaders.
  • Maintain the company's financial model (revenue, expenses, headcount, and cash) and keep the key assumptions up to date. Structure it so that running a new scenario is a configuration change, not a rebuild.
  • Run scenario analysis to help leadership weigh decisions, using AI to build and iterate on cases faster than a manual model rebuild allows, fast enough to be useful in the meeting where the decision is actually being made.

Reporting

  • Own the monthly reporting package: actuals versus budget and forecast, variance analysis, and commentary. AI-drafted first pass, then edited and owned by you.
  • Help prepare materials for leadership and board meetings, including our key metrics and dashboards.
  • Work with the accounting team during month-end close to make sure results are accurate and on time.

Metrics and analysis

  • Own our core SaaS metrics (ARR/MRR, net and gross revenue retention, churn, CAC, and LTV) and keep the definitions consistent.
  • Look at customer, product, and segment profitability and take the findings to the people who can act on them.
  • Build and maintain reports in our BI tools so teams can see the numbers they need, and so that analysts, dashboards and agents all draw on one trusted source rather than several competing ones.

Working with the business

  • Be the finance point of contact for Sales, Marketing, Product, and G&A, helping them manage budgets and understand spend.
  • Partner with Data and Analytics to scope reporting needs, so what we build answers the right questions.
  • Help evaluate the costs and benefits of proposed projects and investments.
  • Handle ad-hoc analysis requests as they come up.

A Little Bit About You

  • A reliable instinct for when a machine-generated answer is wrong. This is a very important qualification for this role.
  • Structured thinking: you can break a vague business question into defined, verifiable steps, which is the same skill that makes an agent work.
  • Demonstrated use of AI tools in real finance work. You can walk us through something you automated or accelerated, and how you checked the output.
  • Experience building AI-assisted workflows: prompt-based reporting, scripting, or connecting AI tools to finance data sources.
  • 3–5+ years of experience in FP&A, corporate finance, or a similar analytical finance role. We weight demonstrated ability to build with AI as heavily as two additional years of conventional experience.
  • Experience at a SaaS or subscription business, or willingness to get up to speed on the model.
  • A good understanding of common SaaS metrics (ARR, retention, churn, CAC, LTV) and what drives them.
  • Solid financial modeling and Excel/Google Sheets skills. Excel and Google Sheets are output formats here rather than the core skill; the core skill is breaking a FP&A question down precisely enough that an agent can run it reliably and repeatably.
  • A working knowledge of the three financial statements and subscription revenue recognition.
  • The ability to explain financial results clearly to people outside of finance.
  • Comfort with ERP, planning, and BI tools (e.g. NetSuite, Cube, QuickSight, or similar).
  • An understanding of how finance and business systems fit together and how data moves between them, and the ability to scope reporting needs with Data teams.
  • A willingness to work in the open, documenting what you build so that someone else can run it.
  • A Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.

Nice to Have

  • Experience partnering with Sales or RevOps on pipeline, quota, or go-to-market planning.
  • Exposure to headcount and workforce planning alongside the People team.
  • SQL or comfort working with larger datasets.
  • MBA, CFA, or CPA.

Our Stack

  • Every employee has a Claude account. Recurly for billing and Rillet for accounting, both implemented this year. QuickSight for business intelligence.

Share Our Values

  • Customer First
  • Bias for Action
  • High Velocity Decision Making
  • Inclusion
  • Results Focused

Compensation

Our compensation bands are designed to reflect how people grow in their roles. Each level includes three stages: Developing, Proficient and Expert, which represent increasing capability, independence and impact over time.

The compensation range for this role is $95,000 to $110,000 CAD which reflects the Proficient stage of our compensation band for this job level (P3). For United States based applicants, the compensation range for this role is $100,000 to $120,000 USD.

Progression into higher stages and job levels may occur over time based on demonstrated performance, mastery of role expectations and overall impact. For specialized or hard-to-fill roles, we may extend offers above the posted range if a candidate brings exceptional experience.

Perks & Benefits

Flexibility and Time Off

  • Flexible Time Off Policy - We encourage a minimum of 4 weeks per year!
  • Remote First Team
  • Flexible Hours
  • Work From Anywhere Program

Health and Wellness

  • Health Insurance
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Quarterly Company Wide Recharge Days
  • End of Year Company Wide Holiday Closure
  • Maternity & Parental Leave Program
  • $2000 Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA)

Growth & Future

  • Professional Development Budget
  • Volunteer Day
  • Team Building Budget
  • Employee Referral Bonus Program ($1000)
  • Anniversary Milestone LSA Top Up
  • Birthday Day Off

We Value Individuality!

At Unbounce, we want every employee to be excited to bring their full, authentic self to work. When you bring your unique experiences, background, knowledge, perspective, and self-expression while embracing the same from others we learn from each other. We innovate and co-create an environment where team members can do the best work of their careers. We're bolder and more brilliant together.

We're dedicated to ensuring each team member feels a sense of belonging, feels safe, cared for, respected and valued for who they are, and trusts that their unique voice is heard, embraced, and meaningfully contributes to decision-making. We're committed to equitable employee experience, opportunity, pay and support for every employee regardless of gender identity or expression, race, ethnicity, family or marital status, religion, socio-economic status, veteran status, national origin, age, sexual orientation, education, disability, or any other characteristic that makes you unique.

We have no tolerance for sexism, racism, xenophobia, homophobia, transphobia, ableism, ageism, or any other forms of hateful/harmful discrimination and we're taking action against unequal pay in our community through leading the #PayUpforProgress movement.

If you require any accommodations or support during the recruitment process, please email us at .

Our use of AI in hiring

We're committed to keeping hiring personal. Every application is reviewed by a real person on our team, and we don't use AI to screen or filter candidates out.

We do use AI to help with assessing candidates and summarizing interview feedback. These tools support our team in working more efficiently and reducing bias. All final hiring decisions are made by people who bring their judgment and experience to determine who joins our team.

jobs.description:
Overview

Since 1972, Covenant House has served and advocated for youth and young families experiencing homelessness, human trafficking, and exploitation. Our overarching goal is to end homelessness among youth and young families by helping them achieve housing stability, heal from trauma, tap into their innate resilience, and hone their interests and skills to forge new pathways to independence. This work is carried out across Covenant House sites in 34 cities in the US, Canada, Mexico, Guatemala, and Honduras.

About the Role

Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Advocacy and Strategic Partnerships, the Vice President of Advocacy and Strategic Partnerships serves as the strategic and operational leader responsible for translating vision into execution across the advocacy portfolio. The VP acts as the SVP's key thought partner and deputy, maintaining visibility across priorities, advancing enterprise alignment, identifying risks and opportunities, building and stewarding key relationships, and ensuring strategic initiatives move from concept to implementation along established timeframes.

This role sits at the intersection of strategy, advocacy, youth leadership, partnership development, and organizational change. The VP will oversee the International Youth Congress (IYC), coordinate implementation of Covenant House's advocacy priorities across the federation and help ensure that advocacy efforts remain aligned with the organization'sStrategic Visionand the Strategy Office’s goals.

Successful candidates are equally comfortable advising senior leaders, facilitating cross-functional collaboration, authentically engaging and lifting up youth with lived experience, managing complex initiatives, and driving day-to-day execution. We’re looking for someone who can operate as a trusted advisor to senior leadership while also rolling up their sleeves to get work done, bringing exceptional project and portfolio management discipline.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Leadership of International Youth Congress (50%)

  • Serve as the organizational lead responsible for successful implementation, institutionalization, and long-term sustainability of the International Youth Congress

  • Ensure IYC recommendations and insights are systematically integrated into organizational planning, policy development, program design, research initiatives, and continuous quality improvement processes

  • Build organizational readiness for meaningful youth partnership across the enterprise

  • Develop governance structures, feedback loops, accountability mechanisms, and decision-making pathways that elevate youth voice while ensuring organizational effectiveness

  • Supervise the Youth Advocacy Program Manager, ensuring consistent, high-quality execution of key logistical and coordination tasks to deliver excellent programming for IYC members

  • Manage the IYC budget and ensure accurate, timely reporting to SVP of Advocacy and Strategic Partnerships

  • Coordinate IYC Advisory Board, ensuring performance indicators for governance and engagement are met

  • Oversee development of IYC curriculum to align with strategic vision implementation

  • Manage vendors and consultants to build IYC capacity and enhance the leadership skills of members

  • Forge partnerships and collaborations with organizations, experts, and stakeholders to expand resources and opportunities for International Youth Congress leadership development

  • Establish key relationships and serve as the point of contact for IYC site leads, fostering understanding of and strong buy-in for IYC across the federation, ensuring consistent understanding of IYC goals, vision, values, and timeline of implementation

  • Partner with Research and Impact team to develop meaningful opportunities for IYC members to participate in research and evaluation studies to advance practice and policy learning related to youth homelessness and other relevant social determinants of health

  • Collaborate across Covenant House teams and departments to ensure strong communication and ongoing institutional support and sustainability

Strategic Leadership & Enterprise Alignment (25%)

  • Serve as primary operational partner and strategic advisor to SVP of Advocacy and Strategic Partnerships

  • Maintain enterprise-wide awareness of advocacy, youth engagement, partnership, prevention and restoration initiatives, proactively identifying opportunities, risks, dependencies, implementation challenges- and proposed solutions

  • Coordinate implementation of advocacy-related priorities within the Advocacy Team workplan

  • Develop and manage systems and processes that ensure accountability, follow-through, buy-in, and visibility on major initiatives

  • Monitor progress toward strategic goals and key performance indicators and regularly provide recommendations to the SVP

  • Lead cross-functional planning efforts and coordinate work across Advocacy, Research & Impact, Development, Communications, IT, Programs, and site leadership

  • Ensure alignment between policy priorities, International Youth Congress initiatives, partnership development, and organizational strategy

  • Support senior leadership decision making through briefings, recommendations, environmental scans, and strategic analyses

  • Facilitate leadership meetings, planning sessions, and implementation reviews as needed

Management of Advocacy Agenda (25%)

  • Support planning and implementation of the International Advocacy Framework, and support enterprise and sites in executing elements of the advocacy agenda as part of larger Prevention Pathway

  • Coordinate advocacy activities across levels to ensure consistency and alignment

  • Establish systems for monitoring policy opportunities, organizational responses, and advocacy outcomes

  • Support federation-wide advocacy planning and implementation through structured communication, technical assistance, and cross-site collaboration as needed

  • Develop briefings and recommendations for leadership on emerging policy issues, risks and opportunities

  • Provide legislative and regulatory analysis and advisement for federal initiatives (E.g., congressional bills, appropriations, and earmarks; executive orders and presidential memorandums; HUD YHDP, YHSI, FYI; ACF RHYTPA; State JTIP; DOJ VOCA; etc.) as well as international and regional opportunities

  • Liaise with policy and advocacy leaders related to ending youth homelessness and child trafficking

  • Collaborate on thought leadership through the (co)authorship of blogs, white papers, policy briefs, and other media to advance Covenant House’s advocacy agenda

  • Cultivate strong relationships with key leaders and decision-makers from partner organizations; this involves regular communication and fostering a collaborative and mutually beneficial partnership

  • Create strong pathways for youth advocacy including participation in policy analysis and development, advocacy skills building and training, and participation in advocacy opportunities, including the annual Covenant House Advocacy Week

  • Support training and technical assistance to Covenant House sites to advance site specific youth advocacy and lived experience initiatives and programs

  • Coordinate with Research and Impact team and Covenant House sites to solicit and receive key performance metrics for advocacy

Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Project management excellence — ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously and consistently deliver high-quality outputs on deadlines

  • Political judgment — discernment of how to effectively assess risk, timing, and stakeholder interests to provide effective recommendations to SVP of advocacy and strategic partnerships

  • Change management — experience helping organizations, teams, and individual contributors adopt and sustain new practices and approaches

  • Relationship management across levels — comfortable engaging CEOs, frontline staff, youth leaders, government officials, and community partners

  • Facilitation and convening expertise — capable of leading workshops, strategy sessions, peer-learning cohorts, and planning processes

  • Data literacy — ability to interpret and communicate data for advocacy, policy analysis, and decision-making

  • Resource development and grant knowledge — familiarity with public funding systems and how policy influences nonprofit financing

  • Cultural humility and intergenerational leadership — experience working effectively with youth, emerging leaders, and senior executives alike

  • Comfort with ambiguity and entrepreneurial environments — able to build systems, iterate for improvement, rapidly apply learning, pivot rapidly, and effectively prioritize

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Teams, Zoom, and project management tools

Required Qualifications

  • Seven plus years’ experience of progressive leadership experience in advocacy, public policy, coalition building, youth development, systems change, nonprofit leadership, or related fields.

  • Demonstrated experience in youth work, including professional evolution from individual/ case-level work to program management and leadership

  • Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from strategy through implementation.

  • Proven experience influencing senior leaders and stakeholders without direct authority

  • Experience developing and executing operational/ implementation plans and performance measures

  • Prior experience managing direct reports

Preferred Knowledge, Skills, Abilities and Qualifications

  • Spanish fluency (oral and written) with strong cross-cultural communication skills strongly preferred

  • Graduate degree in public policy, social work, psychology, sociology or related field. Or equivalent combination of lived, professional, and academic experience.

  • Demonstrated experience supporting policy implementation and/or advocacy initiatives at international and/or federal and national levels

  • Significant knowledge of at least one major social determinant of health policy domain, such as housing and homelessness, behavioral health, workforce development, education, child welfare, poverty reduction, public benefits, violence prevention, or juvenile justice

  • Familiarity with federal legislative and regulatory processes and the mechanics of implementation

  • Experience working with nonprofits, public agencies, coalitions, or cross-sector partnerships

  • Experience navigating politically diverse environments and building bipartisan relationships

Travel Requirements

  • Up to 25%. Ability to travel to New York City for our annual in-person traditions; Strategy Office/ Advocacy Team meetings; Washington D.C., for policy leadership engagements; and throughout our federation as required

  • Outside of above travel, this position is 100% remote

Our Community

Our critical mission demands that we have all voices at the table. A team of diverse people, perspectives, and experiences is smarter, stronger, and more effective for our young people. At Covenant House, every team member is valued, respected, heard, and supported, and we welcome honest and courageous self-reflection on any aspects of our work that are based on biased or outdated viewpoints. We deliberately create opportunities for our staff to grow and thrive.

jobs.description:
Alternative Payments is building the financial operating system for SMBs, consolidating the disconnected tech stack that holds service-based businesses back. Starting with MSPs, we’ve spent five years perfecting accounts receivable, and we’re now expanding into accounts payable, AI-powered analytics, and beyond. We’re at an inflection point: closing the loop on money movement and laying the foundation for a platform that will reshape how service businesses operate financially.

We’re growing fast, thinking big, and building a global team that wants to be part of something that lasts. We believe the best solutions come from diverse perspectives, deep collaboration, and a shared obsession with customer impact. If you’re energized by real problems, real customers, and real impact, we want to hear from you!

What We’re Looking For

We’re seeking a Head of Outbound to own the strategy, execution, and accountability of our outbound sales motion across the MSP and Accounting segments. You’ll design the BDR outbound architecture — signal-based targeting, sequence strategy, cold call frameworks, and email positioning — then build rigor and accountability throughout the team to make sure it runs at a high level every day.

Our BDR team operates in segment-specific pods (SMB, Mid-Market, Accounting), each led by an AE team lead who handles coaching and deal-level training but isn’t directly responsible for day-to-day outbound accountability. Your job is to fill that gap: build what the AE leads teach, set the standard for outbound quality, and drive efficiency improvements that show up in the numbers.

This is a hybrid position requiring a minimum of 4 days in office based in Toronto, ON and is available to candidates who are eligible to work in Canada.

What You’ll Do

  • Improve outbound efficiency across MSP and Accounting segments: diagnose what’s working, redesign what isn’t, and raise the bar on BDR output.

  • Design BDR outbound playbooks for each segment: signal-based targeting, sequence architecture, cold call scripts, and email positioning tailored to different buyer personas.

  • Build rigor and accountability across the BDR team — daily/weekly operating cadences, activity standards, pipeline inspection, and performance management.

  • Collaborate across Marketing, Partnerships, and Events to drive a strategic approach to outbound efforts.

  • Work with Head of New Markets to build GTM plans for new verticals: define the buyer, the pitch, the outbound motion, and the pipeline targets.

  • Build the mid-market and enterprise outbound motion alongside the existing SMB process.

What You’ll Bring

  • 5–10 years in B2B SaaS or fintech sales, including time where your job was building or running outbound programs across multiple segments.

  • Experience building outbound playbooks: signal-based targeting, cold sequences, call frameworks. You know the difference between a sequence that books meetings and one that gets ignored.

  • A track record of improving BDR performance through better process, accountability, and outbound strategy — not just managing reps, but raising the standard.

  • You’ve worked at a company in the $3M–$20M ARR range where not everything was built yet.

  • Working knowledge of Salesforce, Apollo, Instantly.

  • Proven ability to leverage AI to drive team efficiency and prove outcomes with tangible results.

Nice to Haves

  • Familiarity with the MSP / Accounting ecosystem, PE-backed roll-ups, or payments/AR automation.

  • Experience building outbound motions across multiple verticals simultaneously.

  • Comfort with outbound tooling beyond Apollo — intent data platforms, enrichment tools, deliverability monitoring.

  • Track record coaching or mentoring BDRs into AE roles.

  • Deals you personally closed in markets your company hadn’t sold into before.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary tailored to your experience, skills, and expertise.

  • The total compensation range for this role is $225,000 - $250,000 CAD (OTE), plus equity. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the approximate total target compensation for the position. Within the range, individual pay is determined by factors including relevant skills, experience, education/training.

  • Equity opportunities so you can share in our growth and success.

  • Unlimited PTO and flexibility when you need it the most.

  • Yearly learning & development stipend to help you grow and do your best work.

Why Choose Alternative Payments?

At Alternative Payments, you’ll do work that truly matters.

  • Own your impact: Lead meaningful, high-impact projects and collaborative initiatives that are shaping the future of FinTech and redefining how businesses get paid.

  • Collaborate: Work with a diverse, innovative team where every voice is heard and great ideas come from anywhere.

  • Grow with us: Your career journey is top of mind. We prioritize internal growth and give you the space to shape your path based on your goals — whether that’s deepening your expertise in your domain or exploring something new.

  • Thrive in a supportive culture: As a scaling start-up, there’s a lot to be done and initiative is key. We believe in shared learning, open communication, and building each other up. When one of us grows, we all do.

Want to see what we're actually building?

We made a short video so you don't have to take our word for it. Get a glimpse of our product, our people, and the problems we're solving, then decide if it sounds like your kind of place.

Our Values

  • Transparency & Honesty: We communicate openly and truthfully with partners, investors, and each other so everyone understands where we stand and where we’re headed.

  • Resourcefulness & AI: We stay scrappy, find creative solutions, and make progress even when the path isn’t obvious. We have a bias for action and seek out the information and resources necessary to make decisions and move quickly.

  • Partnership: We win and lose together. We collaborate with our partners, investors, and teammates to tackle big challenges and reach shared goals.

  • Revolutionary & Boldness: We challenge conventions, take calculated risks, and build better, stronger solutions that move our business and the industry forward.

  • Accountability: We take ownership of our decisions and results. We follow through on our commitments knowing our work directly impacts our partners, our team and our business.

Applying to Alternative Payments

We’re looking for candidates who are ready to step in and make an impact from day one. We know that sometimes people hold back unless they meet every requirement, but if you’re excited about the role, bring relevant experience, and are ready to contribute, we want to hear from you!

All resumes are reviewed by our small but mighty talent team. While we may use AI tools to help prioritize applications, real people are behind every resume review and hiring decision. We’re also committed to an inclusive and accessible process. If you need any accommodations during your application or interview experience, please let us know — we’re happy to help.

jobs.description:
Company Summary:

Slang AI is redefining customer engagement through conversational AI, making every interaction seamless and efficient. Our mission is to transform the restaurant industry by providing the ultimate voice AI solution for consistently outstanding customer experiences. At Slang AI, we foster a culture of innovation, inclusivity, and growth, ensuring that every "Slangsta" (employee) feels valued and connected to our broader AI driven impact.

What Your Experience Will Be:

As a Client Experience Manager at Slang AI, you’ll own the end-to-end customer journey for our SMB clients — from onboarding through long-term success and day-to-day support. You’ll guide customers through their initial rollout, transition seamlessly into serving as their long-term success manager, and directly manage the support inbox during business hours, where many of their most important interactions occur.
Because support volume is currently low (fewer than 60 inquiries per month across 1,500+ customers), this role offers the opportunity to both deliver excellent frontline support and help design how support scales as we grow. You’ll gain unique visibility into customer needs in real time while influencing the tools, processes, and standards that will shape support as the business expands.
This unique scope means you’ll be both a strategic advisor and a hands-on partner, ensuring customers launch smoothly, adopt key features, resolve challenges quickly, and realize the full value of Slang. By owning these critical touch points, you’ll have a large sphere of influence over customer outcomes, shaping retention, adoption, and satisfaction across a significant segment of the business.
In addition, you’ll play a key role in our digital customer success program — helping define and refine automated success sequences to ensure accuracy, consistency, and strong adoption results. This work ensures customers experience the same hospitality-first service at scale, while giving you a direct impact on how Slang drives measurable results for our clients.

Why You Belong Here & How You Will Grow:

At Slang, we believe success starts with great execution and great service. In this role, you’ll gain valuable experience managing full customer lifecycles and working with hospitality operators in a fast-paced environment. You’ll learn how to onboard, support, and grow a book of business with autonomy, while contributing to scalable processes that improve outcomes across the team. We offer training, feedback, and growth opportunities to help you level up in customer success, technical product fluency, and strategic account management.

What Success Looks Like

  • Driving Long-Term Success: You are responsible for the health and success of your assigned accounts. You ensure customers are seeing clear outcomes, meeting their goals, and staying on track for renewal.
  • Building Trusted Relationship: You build strong relationships with a range of customer stakeholders — from General Managers to Operations Leaders — and know how to tailor your approach depending on their needs.
  • Renewals & Retention: You own the renewal process and are accountable for maintaining and growing account revenue. You identify risks early, take action to resolve issues, and keep customers satisfied and committed.
  • Surfacing Growth Opportunity: You surface expansion opportunities (e.g. additional locations or use cases) and work with Sales to execute. You contribute to the team’s Net Revenue Retention (NRR) goal.
  • Feature Adoption & Product Fluency: You guide customers through product updates, encourage usage of key features, and tie adoption back to business outcomes. You’re expected to understand and explain Slang’s value.
  • Onboarding and Success Planning: You create simple account plans to track customer goals, key contacts, risks, and growth potential. You align internal teams around each plan to support execution.
  • Voice of the Customer: You escalate customer feedback internally and contribute insights that improve product and service. You partner with Product and Support to advocate for customer needs.
  • Hospitality-First Service: You respond quickly, handle challenges with professionalism, and make interactions easy for customers. You aim to create a positive experience in every conversation.

What You Will Bring

  • Customer Focus: You care about helping customers succeed. You’re responsive, thoughtful, and proactive.
  • Experience: 3+ years of experience in customer success, account management, or client-facing roles. Background in restaurants or hospitality tech is strongly preferred.
  • Business Acumen: You understand restaurant operations and how to align Slang’s value with business goals. You’re comfortable working with executives and frontline staff alike.
  • Communication: You’re clear and concise in both written and verbal communication. You know how to explain ideas, give updates, and lead customer conversations.
  • Ownership: You manage your book of business with attention to detail. You’re accountable for renewals, engagement, and outcomes.
  • Adaptability: You’re comfortable in a fast-changing environment and open to feedback. You handle ambiguity and know how to prioritize.
  • Preferred: Experience with restaurant operations, phone systems, or reservation platforms is a plus.

How Work Affects My Life:

As a Client Experience Manager for SMBs, you’ll directly contribute to the success of hospitality teams. Your work helps restaurant staff be more productive, improve guest service, and hit their business goals. In return, Slang supports you with competitive pay, benefits, and a culture that values performance and teamwork. You’ll have clear goals, a meaningful role, and the opportunity to grow.

Our Vision

Calling a business shouldn’t feel like a robot-hostage situation, where you’re forced to listen to horrible music and can't reach a human, while enduring a soulless voice uttering "I'm sorry I didn't quite get that" on repeat for eternity. (shudder) That’s why we started Slang.ai. We use the latest AI and audio wizardry to make transacting via voice so enjoyable it’s more human than human. By 2030, we will save businesses and consumers 1 billion minutes of precious time while transforming voice channels into the preferred mode of communication (it's faster and easier than text).
We have backgrounds building product at companies like Spotify, Buzzfeed, the New York Times, and OpenTable —shipping experiences that have reached hundreds of millions of users. Now, we’re using our backgrounds to start a new culture, one that puts product and human-centered design above all else while fostering constant learning and growth. Sound like something you’d like to be part of? Get on board.

Our Values

Overachiever Fever. We’re overachievers (we don’t know any other way)
Learner Fervor. We take every opportunity to learn (especially when it’s hard)
Humility Ability. We approach each other with curiosity and openness (know-it-alls not welcome!)
SMB MVP. We’re an expert member of our customers’ teams (we earn their trust)

jobs.description:
Role Summary:

The Manager, Quality – Digital Systems is a business-facing role that serves as the primary point of contact between RQA’s digital quality systems and the stakeholders who depend on them, with working technical depth in Veeva eQMS administration and GxP-regulated system operations anchoring that work. This role is accountable for the reliable administration and continuous improvement of Veeva eQMS processes, including access management, business administration, release coordination, and reporting. The successful candidate will bring enough configuration fluency - understanding vault object relationships, shared versus instance-specific configuration, and the downstream consequences of proposed system changes - to translate technical trade-offs into clear guidance for stakeholders and support faster, better-informed decisions on enhancement requests and system design questions.

The successful candidate must communicate clearly across technical and business audiences, understand stakeholder needs, assess business and technical trade-offs, and support technology decisions that advance quality operations and broader business objectives. Beyond day-to-day operations, this role independently represents the RQA Digital Systems team within cross-functional programs and enterprise initiatives, scoping RQA’s responsibilities within a given program and developing and driving the execution plan on behalf of the team. This role operates with a high degree of autonomy, maintaining clear situational awareness across assigned responsibilities and bringing issues and decisions forward proactively.

This position requires strong communication and analytical skills, working Veeva domain knowledge, genuine curiosity about applying AI and emerging technology to quality operations, and the ability to operate effectively in a regulated pharmaceutical environment — both as a business partner and as an accountable owner of complex, cross-functional work.

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES:

Veeva eQMS Operations & Administration

  • Serve as the primary business administrator for Veeva eQMS on behalf of Regulatory Quality Assurance.

  • Triage and resolvebusiness admin requests requiring business-level judgment, partnering with technical teams on complex issues.

  • Own access request intake and provisioning across RQA’s digital systems environments.

  • Support Veeva release coordination through UAT, business approvals and communications, and production deployments.

  • Maintain and continuously improve job aids, quick reference guides, and user-facing documentation for Veeva eQMS and integrated supporting tools, keeping materials current across system releases.

  • Develop, prepare, and deliver reporting across functional areas.

eQMS Systems Expertise & Advisory

  • Provide guidance on Veeva vault configuration options in support of business needs, including object relationships, shared configuration dependencies, and the downstream impact of proposed changes, partnering with technical teams to fill configuration depth as needed.

  • Support the triage and formulation of eQMS enhancement requests, providing business context and impact assessment alongside stakeholder needs and operational impacts to inform prioritization and decision-making.

  • Stay current on Veeva platform developments and GxP digital systems best practices, especially with respect to emerging AI technologies, applying that knowledge to identify and champion opportunities to modernize system design and operations.

  • Participate in eQMS governance forums, representing RQA Digital Systems’ interests and staying current on platform developments.

Cross-Functional Program Support

  • Independently represent the RQA Digital Systems team within enterprise programs and initiatives requiring digital systems support, scoping team responsibilities, developing execution plans, and delivering against them.

  • Maintain clear ownership of workstream status and decisions; proactively surface blockers or escalation points to leadership.

  • Coordinate with Pfizer Digital and cross-functional teams to support enterprise quality data integrity and system continuity efforts.

Reporting & Data Operations

  • Issue clear and timely communications, ensuring stakeholders are informed and aligned on timelines and expected outcomes.

  • Execute periodic data extracts and reporting tasks, including basic dashboarding and data queries, in support of regulatory and quality operations, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and appropriate documentation.

  • Develop and maintain operational documentation and user guidance for current and legacy quality systems to ensure operational continuity.

  • Gather, synthesize, and prepare materials for stakeholder communications and leadership briefings, translating system and data insights into accessible formats.

Transformation & Continuous Improvement

  • Proactively identify opportunities for meaningful process improvement and digital transformation within RQA’s quality systems operations, bringing both technical grounding and operational context to proposed solutions.

  • Apply practical AI knowledge to evaluate use cases, partner with technical teams, and drive adoption of AI-enabled solutions.

  • Contribute to and support broader organizational transformation initiatives, including AI integration into quality workflows, eQMS process redesign, and platform evolution.

  • Stay current on Veeva platform capabilities, GxP digital systems trends, and regulatory expectations, applying emerging best practices to improve the team’s operations and delivery.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences, Information Systems, Computer Science or a related field with 5+ years of relevant industry experience; advanced degree preferred.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to produce clear documentation, user-facing guidance, and stakeholder-ready reports.

  • Demonstrated experience working directly and iteratively with business stakeholders to understand their underlying needs and workflows.

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Our Commitment to Authenticity

jobs.excerpt: What We Can Achieve Together:The Finance Manager works within the Southern Division business unit and serves as the primary finance partner for the Southern Division Office and programs housed within the Division.
jobs.description:
What We Can Achieve Together:

The Finance Manager works within the Southern Division business unit and serves as the primary finance partner for the Southern Division Office and programs housed within the Division. The portfolio currently includes the financial management of the Southern Division Office, North American Fire and the Mississippi River Basin Program. Additional programs may be added as appropriate.

This is a hands-on finance leadership role that combines day-to-day financial management with strategic financial planning and decision support. The Finance Manager is expected to independently manage core financial activities, including journal entries, account reconciliations, reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and year-end close, while also applying strong financial judgment to identify opportunities, evaluate alternatives, develop recommendations, and help shape funding and resource allocation strategies.

The Finance Manager partners closely with program and Division leaders, conservation, philanthropy, operations, grants, and other functional teams to provide strategic financial guidance, high-level analysis, and informed decision support. The Manager serves as a trusted finance thought partner, helping translate organizational and programmatic priorities into effective financial strategies and actionable plans.

In addition to managing the finances of the Southern Division Office and its programs, the Finance Manager serves the broader Southern Division as a finance resource and thought partner. The role provides financial guidance, consultation, problem-solving, and analysis to leaders and teams across the Division as needs arise. The Finance Manager reports directly to the Southern Division Finance Director and works closely with the North American Fire Program Director through a strong dotted-line relationship to support the financial management needs of North American Fire. This matrixed structure requires close coordination, clear communication, and shared partnership with program and Division leadership. The Manager also collaborates with other finance leaders at the Division level to advance divisional priorities, strengthen financial management practices, and promote consistency, collaboration, and operational excellence across the Southern Division.

This position is expected to evolve with the organization. As the Southern Division Office and its programs grow in size, funding, complexity, and financial management needs, the scope and responsibilities of the position may expand accordingly.

We're Looking for You:

The Finance Manager provides strategic financial management and serves as a trusted advisor to leaders and teams within the Southern Division Office and programs housed within the Division. The role leads financial planning, forecasting, reporting, analysis, stewardship, and day-to-day financial management activities that support informed decision-making and long-term financial sustainability.

The Finance Manager is expected to operate with a high degree of independence, using financial expertise and organizational judgment to assess situations, identify issues and opportunities, develop options and recommendations, and determine appropriate courses of action. The role does not simply report financial information or execute established processes; it interprets financial information, connects it to programmatic and organizational priorities, and proactively brings forward recommendations for leadership consideration.

The Manager translates financial information into actionable insight, helping leaders understand financial performance, assess risks and opportunities, evaluate alternatives, and make informed resource allocation decisions. The role establishes and maintains effective financial practices and controls while contributing to broader financial strategy, funding decisions, and resource allocation across the Division.

The Manager also serves as a finance resource to the broader Southern Division, providing consultation, analysis, problem-solving, and thought partnership to state and program leaders when Division needs arise.

Location: This role is remote with preference to the Eastern or Central time zones.

Travel: This role will travel as required to attend in-person trainings, retreats, or other events. Travel is not expected to exceed 10% annually.

RESPONSIBILITIES & SCOPE

  • Manage day-to-day financial activities for the assigned portfolio, including journal entries, account reconciliations, financial transactions, reporting, budget maintenance, year-end close activities, and other core financial management processes.

  • Serve as the primary finance partner for the Southern Division Office and programs housed within the Division, currently including North American Fire and the Mississippi River Basin Program, providing financial leadership across budgeting, forecasting, reporting, analysis, resource planning, and financial stewardship. Additional programs may be added as appropriate.

  • Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, long-range financial planning, financial reporting, fiscal year-end activities, and other financial management initiatives for the assigned portfolio.

  • Deliver high-quality financial reporting, complex financial analysis, scenario modeling, and recommendations that enable program and Division leaders to understand financial performance, assess risks and opportunities, and make informed decisions regarding resources and priorities.

  • Independently analyze financial information and develop recommendations regarding budgets, forecasts, funding, resource allocation, spending strategies, and financial risks and opportunities.

  • Translate organizational and programmatic priorities into financial strategies and actionable plans, helping leaders evaluate tradeoffs and determine how available resources can have the greatest organizational and conservation impact.

  • Proactively identify financial issues, opportunities, and emerging needs and bring forward well-developed options and recommendations to the Southern Division Finance Director and program leadership. Follow through on agreed strategies and decisions through implementation and ongoing monitoring.

  • Serve as a finance thought partner to program and Division leaders.

  • Serve as an active member of the leadership teams of the Southern Division Office, North American Fire, and The Mississippi River Basin Program, participating in leadership meetings, planning discussions, retreats, and other forums to provide financial perspective and contribute to programmatic and strategic decision-making.

  • Develop sufficient understanding of the goals, funding models, operations, and financial needs of multiple programs to effectively balance competing priorities and provide relevant financial guidance across the portfolio.

  • Serve as a finance resource and thought partner to leaders and teams across the broader Southern Division, providing consultation, problem-solving, financial analysis, and guidance on financial management issues as Division needs arise, as well as promote consistent financial practices to strengthen financial management across the Southern Division.

  • Support Division-level resource allocation and funding strategies, including analyzing available funding, evaluating alternative uses of resources, partnering with state Business Units and programs to identify opportunities and constraints, and developing recommendations that balance financial sustainability, organizational priorities, and conservation impact.

  • Identify financial risks and opportunities, evaluate alternatives, and develop recommendations to strengthen financial performance, optimize resource allocation, and achieve organizational objectives.

  • Ensure effective stewardship of financial resources through strong internal controls, compliance with organizational policies, donor and funding requirements, regulatory standards, and generally accepted accounting principles, as applicable.

  • Ensure the accuracy, integrity, and effective management of financial data, processes, and controls, including appropriate use of Workday and other financial systems.

  • Partner with philanthropy, conservation, operations, grants, government relations, leadership, and other functional teams to provide financial guidance for fundraising initiatives, grants, contracts, campaigns, and strategic projects.

  • Support financial management of federal awards and other restricted funding, working in partnership with grants and program teams to ensure appropriate budgeting, financial monitoring, reporting, and compliance.

  • Oversee financial aspects of contracts, agreements, and other business transactions, ensuring compliance with organizational policies and sound financial practices.

  • Serve as the Certified Contract Specialist for the Southern Division Office, as assigned, supporting contract development, review, execution, monitoring, and compliance in accordance with organizational requirements.

  • Support governance and leadership activities by serving as a financial resource to Division leadership, program leadership, Boards of Trustees, Finance Committees, and other stakeholder groups, as appropriate.

  • Partner with the Southern Division Finance Director to implement financial strategies, strengthen financial management practices, promote consistency across the Division, and support continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Contribute to the development and implementation of financial processes, tools, and practices that can scale as the Southern Division Office and its programs grow in size, funding, and complexity.

  • Build and maintain trusted partnerships across the Division and Programs, fostering collaboration, financial accountability, and shared ownership of financial outcomes.

While TNC supports work-life balance, there may be periods of increased workload requiring additional hours and flexibility to meet critical deadlines and organizational priorities.

What You'll Bring:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or related field and 4 years' related experience or equivalent combination.

  • Experience working with computer and information management systems, Excel spreadsheets, and databases for financial analysis, fiscal management, and/or financial reporting.

  • Experience developing budgets, performing high-level financial analysis, recommending actions, and providing financial partnership to leadership.

  • Experience serving as a financial consultant, advisor, or thought partner to organizational leaders and decision-makers.

  • Experience with accounting principles, practices, and regulations.

  • Experience using accounting and financial reporting systems.

  • Experience with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).

  • Experience developing, managing, and implementing multiple projects or financial initiatives.

  • Experience, coursework, or other training with U.S. Federal Uniform Guidance, state and local regulations, multilateral and international regulations, and standard contract clauses, as applicable.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience serving as a strategic finance partner and thought partner to business, program, or organizational leaders.

  • Advanced experience in financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, financial analysis, and translating financial data into actionable recommendations.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently assess financial and operational issues, develop thoughtful recommendations, and move from analysis to action with appropriate consultation and oversight.

  • Demonstrated strategic thinking and ability to connect financial information to organizational priorities, programmatic goals, funding opportunities, and resource allocation decisions.

  • Demonstrated success analyzing complex financial information, identifying risks and opportunities, evaluating alternatives, and developing solutions to improve financial performance and outcomes.

  • Experience supporting financial management across complex programs, portfolios, projects, grants, contracts, or restricted funding sources.

  • Experience developing financial strategies and recommendations in situations where there is not a predetermined solution or established process, requiring sound judgment, initiative, and collaboration.

  • Demonstrated ability to build strong partnerships, influence decision-making, and collaborate effectively across multiple business units, programs, and functional areas.

  • Experience providing financial consultation and problem-solving support outside of one's immediate portfolio or area of responsibility.

  • Demonstrated ability to build credibility and effectively partner with multiple teams or programs, quickly learn different operational and financial environments, and balance competing priorities.

  • Ability to operate effectively in a matrixed organization, serving multiple leaders and programs while maintaining clear priorities, accountability, and communication.

  • Experience evaluating financial processes, internal controls, and management practices to ensure effective stewardship of resources and compliance with organizational policies and applicable regulations.

  • Strong knowledge of GAAP, financial management principles, and relevant regulatory frameworks, with the ability to interpret and apply requirements.

  • Experience working with federal grants, government regulations, contracts, or other restricted funding sources preferred.

  • Experience using enterprise financial systems, including prior experience with Workday or similar ERP systems.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate financial concepts clearly to non-finance audiences and influence decisions through effective financial storytelling.

  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic and evolving environment.

  • Experience working in a collaborative, multi-disciplinary, or mission-driven organization.

  • Multilingual skills and/or multicultural experience appreciated.

  • MBA, CPA, CIA, or other relevant professional certification.

This description is not designed to be a complete list of all duties and responsibilities required for this job.

Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits.
